21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40:

42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)

66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73: 
74: ---

76: ## 2. FRONTMATTER REQUIREMENTS
77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |
83: | `description` | ✅ | Single line, **≤ 130 chars** for skills (≤ 110 for commands), 1,536-char hard cap | `"Handles X when Y occurs"` |
84: | `allowed-tools` | ✅ | Array: `[Tool1, Tool2]` | `[Read, Write, Edit, Bash]` |
85: | `version` | ✅ | 4-part X.Y.Z.W | `1.0.0.0` |
86:

88:

101: ---
102: ```

14: # README Template and Selection Guide
15: 
16: Use this template for project, skill, feature and component READMEs. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) for source-folder READMEs that explain package topology, files, boundaries and data or control flow.

19: 
20: ## 1. README SELECTION
21: 
22: README files answer two questions: what is this, and how does someone use or navigate it?
23: 
24: | Type | Use When | Template |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | Project | The repository or package needs a public entry point | This file |
27: | Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
28: | Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
29: | Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |
31: 
32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.
33: 
34: ```text
35: Is this a project, package, skill or feature root?
36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?
38:     +-- Yes: use readme_code_template.md.
39:     `-- No: write a focused README only if readers need setup, usage or navigation help.
40: ```
41: 
42: Keep READMEs current-state only. Do not cite spec packet numbers, phase IDs or migration history. Use feature names, file paths, commands and stable source links.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE
47: 
48: Use only the sections that fit the audience. Project and skill READMEs often need most sections. Feature and component READMEs should stay shorter.
49: 
50: | Section | Include When | Content |

15: 
16: > Give any external AI assistant the project's full runtime in one dispatch: every plugin, skill and registered MCP server, plus parallel detached sessions for ablation and worker farms.

18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
21: 
22: | Aspect | What you get |
23: |---|---|
24: | **Use it for** | One-shot dispatch into the project's full plugin, skill and MCP runtime, plus parallel detached sessions and cross-AI handback |

29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
36: 
37: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.
38: 
39: ### Why This Skill Exists
40: 
41: An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
42: 
43: ### The Dispatch Surface
44: 
45: | Capability | What the skill can operate |
46: |---|---|
47: | **One-shot full-runtime dispatch** | `opencode run` loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there |
48: | **Parallel detached sessions** | separate session ids and state in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database for ablation suites and worker farms |
49: | **Cross-AI handback** | bridges the dispatch result back into the caller's spec folder through the Memory Handback |
50: | **Provider and model surface** | reaches every configured provider catalog through `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster |
51: | **Agent delegation** | routes to project-local agents under `.skilled/agents/` with the primary-versus-subagent caveats in `references/agent-delegation.md` |
52: 
53: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version. OpenCode 1 is supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. QUICK START
58: 
59: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
60: 
61: ```bash
62: command -v opencode2 || command -v opencode
63: ```
64: 
65: If nothing prints, install with `brew install opencode` (macOS) or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`. On the recommended layout `opencode` is OpenCode 2 and `opencode1` is the OpenCode 1 fallback. A machine with only OpenCode 1 answers to `opencode`.
66: 
67: **Step 2: Run the provider auth pre-flight.**
68: 
69: ```bash
70: opencode providers list
71: ```
72: 
73: Expected when configured: a table of providers with status and default indicators. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), the skill asks before falling back rather than substituting a model you did not approve.
74: 
75: **Step 3: Run the default dispatch.**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: # On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the expected version:
79: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run --standalone \
80:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
81:   --format json \
82:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
83:   </dev/null
84: ```
85: 
86: ```bash
87: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
88: opencode run \
89:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max \
90:   --format json \
91:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
92:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
93:   </dev/null
94: ```
95: 
96: The two versions do not always list the same providers, so on OpenCode 2 check that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m` first. OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider on this machine, and the `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent on OpenCode 1, so `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is the single default on both versions.
97: 
98: You get structured JSON events streamed to stdout as the session runs: `step_start`, `tool_use`, `text` and `step_finish`, every one carrying a `sessionID`, with the reply text in `text` events. The `</dev/null` is mandatory on non-interactive runs on both versions, because the hang is observed on OpenCode 1 and unverified on OpenCode 2. Do not pass top-level `--agent` by default: `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` are subagents that route through a primary path (or, for `ai-council`, through its own `/deep:ai-council` command). Top-level `--agent` is only conditionally allowed for primary agents such as `plan` or `orchestrate` after `opencode run --help` confirms acceptance. When a specific agent profile matters, describe it in the prompt body instead, as this example does.
99: 
100: **Step 4: Spawn a parallel detached session (inside OpenCode only).**
101: 
102: > **Do not pass `--share`.** OpenCode 2 `run` has no such flag. On OpenCode 1.19.3 (fallback) it is a hidden, deprecated flag that prints "Session sharing has been discontinued" and publishes nothing.
103: 
104: ```bash
105: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
106: opencode run --port 4096 \
107:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
108:   "Run a parallel research branch for the approved spec folder." \
109:   </dev/null &
110: ```
111: 
112: On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
113: 
114: The session runs under its own session id in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database (`opencode.db`, `storage/`, `snapshot/`), inspectable independently via `opencode export <sessionID>`. On OpenCode 2 there is no share URL because `run` has no share flag, and on OpenCode 1.19.3 `--share` is a deprecated no-op that publishes nothing.
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
119: 
120: ### The Dispatch Lifecycle
121: 
122: The calling AI composes a prompt, passes it through the smart router to load matching references, then dispatches `opencode run` with an explicit model, variant, format and directory. OpenCode starts a session that loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there. The calling AI parses the JSON event stream incrementally, validates the output and integrates it. The whole round-trip is non-interactive: send the prompt, get the response, exit.
123: 
124: ### The Full-Runtime Difference
125: 
126: This is what sets cli-opencode apart from every sibling in the cli-* family. A sibling dispatch sends a raw model behind a thin CLI wrapper, with no plugins, no skills and no MCP tools. `opencode run` loads the project wholesale. One command gives the dispatched session the skill advisor, Code Mode's external-service manuals, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every project-specific plugin. That is the reason you reach for this skill when the task needs project context rather than a model alone.
127: 
128: ### The Two Non-Obvious Rules
129: 
130: Two `opencode run` defaults punish operators who learn them the hard way.
131: 
132: **Rule 1: use `--agent` deliberately.** The live dispatch contract does not support direct top-level routing to `context`, `review`, `debug` or the other subagents the roster names. None of them is directly invokable as a top-level `opencode run --agent` route. Do not pass `--agent general`. The default path is selected by omitting `--agent`. Some small-model paths documented in `SKILL.md` carry narrower omit-agent caveats.
133: 
134: **Rule 2: append `</dev/null` to every non-interactive run.** Without closed stdin, `opencode run` hangs at zero percent CPU after the snapshot-cleanup line. A foreground `| tail` bypasses this because the upstream pipe stage provides closed stdin, but `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` does not. Position `</dev/null` after the prompt argument, before the redirects.
135: 
136: ### The Self-Invocation Guard
137: 
138: If the agent reading this skill is already inside OpenCode, the skill refuses to load. The guard checks three layers in order:
139: 
140: 1. The `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` env var and any `OPENCODE_*`-prefixed vars, which OpenCode sets on session start.
141: 2. Process ancestry, where an `opencode` parent in the tree trips the guard.
142: 3. A best-effort lock-file probe under `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock`, a heuristic layer since that path does not exist on every install.
143: 
144: The one exception is an explicit parallel detached request. When the prompt contains "parallel detached", "ablation suite", "worker farm" or "spawn detached", the guard allows the dispatch because it spawns a separate session id, not a self-dispatch.
145: 
146: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight
147: 
148: Before the first dispatch in a session the skill checks each provider on OpenCode 2 by filtering `opencode models --standalone` for the `<provider-id>/` prefix, or, on OpenCode 1 (fallback), with `opencode models <provider-id>`. The providers, their models and their effort ceilings live in `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster. Restating them here is how the two copies come to disagree. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions) the skill asks before falling back and never substitutes a model you did not approve. The full roster and effort map live in `references/providers-and-models.md`.
149: 
150: ### Agent Delegation

A non-Anthropic CLI that needs OpenCode as a bridge to a project subsystem such as spec-kit or the skill advisor also lands here. Skip it for simple tasks the caller can answer directly, for raw model dispatch where a sibling cli-* is leaner, for the interactive OpenCode TUI and for anything a plain shell command already covers.

223: The cli-X skills each dispatch to a different provider and never overlap.

228: | `cli-claude-code` | Anthropic | Deep reasoning, diff-based edits, `--json-schema` output, agent delegation |

247:

249: |---|---|---|
250: | `command not found: opencode` | CLI not installed or PATH not updated | `brew install opencode` or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install \| bash`, then restart your terminal |
251: | Dispatch hangs at 0% CPU after the snapshot line | Missing `</dev/null` on a non-interactive run | Append `</dev/null` before any `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` redirect |
252: | `--agent general` fails or warns | The default path is selected by omitting `--agent` | Omit `--agent general`. Use `orchestrate` only when it is the documented primary route and help-verified. Route `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` through the documented primary path (or, for `ai-council`, `/deep:ai-council`) instead of a direct top-level `--agent`. |
253: | `provider/model not found` or `401 Unauthorized` | The default provider is not configured on this machine (`llmgateway` on both versions) | Run `opencode providers list` (OpenCode 1) or `opencode models --standalone` (OpenCode 2), then log in the missing provider |
254: | Empty event stream | Output format defaulted to formatted instead of JSON | Force `--format json` |
255: | `Self-invocation refused` | The caller is already inside OpenCode (`OPENCODE_*` env, `opencode` ancestry or a state lock) | Use a different runtime, exit the current session or restate with explicit parallel-detached keywords |
256: | Unknown `--variant` flag on OpenCode 1 | Binary older than the documented baseline | Run `opencode --version` and `opencode run --help`, then upgrade. It has no `run` form on OpenCode 2. See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md) |
257: | Context too large or truncated | The prompt references broad paths instead of specific files | Split large tasks and use `--file` for attachments |

261: ## 8. FAQ
262: 
263: **Q: What does the full-runtime dispatch buy over a sibling cli-* skill?**
264: 
265: A: A sibling cli-* skill dispatches to a single provider's binary. cli-opencode dispatches into a session that loads every plugin, skill and registered MCP server for the project. When the task needs a project-local skill, a project-specific plugin or the skill advisor, only cli-opencode provides all of them in one shot. When it only needs a model, a sibling is leaner.
266: 
267: **Q: When do I need a parallel detached session?**
268: 
269: A: When you are inside OpenCode and want a second session with its own state and session id. Common patterns are an ablation suite across sessions, a worker farm for parallel research and a cross-repo research branch. On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md). The prompt must contain explicit parallel-session keywords or the self-invocation guard blocks the dispatch.
270: 
271: **Q: Why no top-level `--agent`?**
272: 
273: A: OpenCode 2 accepts `--agent general`. OpenCode 1 (fallback) treats named agents like `general` as subagents and will not run them at the top level: it prints a warning, falls back to the default agent and exits 0, so the flag does not select the requested agent. The default agent already covers the general case. For a specific profile, describe the role in the prompt body.
274: 
275: **Q: Why does a non-interactive dispatch hang without `</dev/null`?**
276: 
277: A: OpenCode reads stdin at startup before session creation. When stdout and stderr are redirected to files, stdin stays open and the process waits forever. Appending `</dev/null` provides an immediate EOF so the dispatch continues.
278: 
279: **Q: Which model do I pick?**
280: 
281: A: Default to `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on both versions. On OpenCode 2 (the expected version) the default is `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`, through the same gateway, because v2 lists no `opencode-go` provider unless it is logged in separately. On OpenCode 1 (fallback) that is `--model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max`, through the DevPass LLM Gateway, which fronts the latency-optimized reasoning model at its max thinking tier. The `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent, so that route hangs on "Go usage limit exceeded". One provider now serves both versions. Switch to `minimax/MiniMax-M3` for MiniMax Direct or `openai/gpt-6-sol` for paid premium. The full roster lives in `references/providers-and-models.md`.

14: # cli-opencode
15: 
16: > Give any external AI assistant the project's full runtime in one dispatch: every plugin, skill and registered MCP server, plus parallel detached sessions for ablation and worker farms.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
21: 
22: | Aspect | What you get |
23: |---|---|
24: | **Use it for** | One-shot dispatch into the project's full plugin, skill and MCP runtime, plus parallel detached sessions and cross-AI handback |
25: | **Invoke with** | "delegate to opencode", "opencode run", "parallel detached", "cross-ai handback" or auto-routing on OpenCode keywords |

27: | **Produces** | Structured JSON event streams, code changes with full project context, parallel research sessions and cross-AI handback results |
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
36: 
37: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.
38: 
39: ### Why This Skill Exists
40: 
41: An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
42: 
43: ### The Dispatch Surface
44: 
45: | Capability | What the skill can operate |
46: |---|---|
47: | **One-shot full-runtime dispatch** | `opencode run` loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there |
48: | **Parallel detached sessions** | separate session ids and state in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database for ablation suites and worker farms |
49: | **Cross-AI handback** | bridges the dispatch result back into the caller's spec folder through the Memory Handback |
50: | **Provider and model surface** | reaches every configured provider catalog through `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster |
51: | **Agent delegation** | routes to project-local agents under `.skilled/agents/` with the primary-versus-subagent caveats in `references/agent-delegation.md` |
52: 
53: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version. OpenCode 1 is supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 3. QUICK START
58: 
59: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
60: 
61: ```bash
62: command -v opencode2 || command -v opencode
63: ```
64: 
65: If nothing prints, install with `brew install opencode` (macOS) or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`. On the recommended layout `opencode` is OpenCode 2 and `opencode1` is the OpenCode 1 fallback. A machine with only OpenCode 1 answers to `opencode`.
66: 
67: **Step 2: Run the provider auth pre-flight.**
68: 
69: ```bash
70: opencode providers list
71: ```
72: 
73: Expected when configured: a table of providers with status and default indicators. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), the skill asks before falling back rather than substituting a model you did not approve.
74: 
75: **Step 3: Run the default dispatch.**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: # On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the expected version:
79: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run --standalone \
80:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
81:   --format json \
82:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
83:   </dev/null
84: ```
85: 
86: ```bash
87: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
88: opencode run \
89:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max \
90:   --format json \
91:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
92:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
93:   </dev/null
94: ```
95: 
96: The two versions do not always list the same providers, so on OpenCode 2 check that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m` first. OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider on this machine, and the `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent on OpenCode 1, so `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is the single default on both versions.
97: 
98: You get structured JSON events streamed to stdout as the session runs: `step_start`, `tool_use`, `text` and `step_finish`, every one carrying a `sessionID`, with the reply text in `text` events. The `</dev/null` is mandatory on non-interactive runs on both versions, because the hang is observed on OpenCode 1 and unverified on OpenCode 2. Do not pass top-level `--agent` by default: `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` are subagents that route through a primary path (or, for `ai-council`, through its own `/deep:ai-council` command). Top-level `--agent` is only conditionally allowed for primary agents such as `plan` or `orchestrate` after `opencode run --help` confirms acceptance. When a specific agent profile matters, describe it in the prompt body instead, as this example does.
99: 
100: **Step 4: Spawn a parallel detached session (inside OpenCode only).**
101: 
102: > **Do not pass `--share`.** OpenCode 2 `run` has no such flag. On OpenCode 1.19.3 (fallback) it is a hidden, deprecated flag that prints "Session sharing has been discontinued" and publishes nothing.
103: 
104: ```bash
105: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
106: opencode run --port 4096 \
107:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
108:   "Run a parallel research branch for the approved spec folder." \
109:   </dev/null &
110: ```
111: 
112: On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
113: 
114: The session runs under its own session id in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database (`opencode.db`, `storage/`, `snapshot/`), inspectable independently via `opencode export <sessionID>`. On OpenCode 2 there is no share URL because `run` has no share flag, and on OpenCode 1.19.3 `--share` is a deprecated no-op that publishes nothing.

117: 
118: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
119: 
120: ### The Dispatch Lifecycle
121: 
122: The calling AI composes a prompt, passes it through the smart router to load matching references, then dispatches `opencode run` with an explicit model, variant, format and directory. OpenCode starts a session that loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there. The calling AI parses the JSON event stream incrementally, validates the output and integrates it. The whole round-trip is non-interactive: send the prompt, get the response, exit.
123: 
124: ### The Full-Runtime Difference
125: 
126: This is what sets cli-opencode apart from every sibling in the cli-* family. A sibling dispatch sends a raw model behind a thin CLI wrapper, with no plugins, no skills and no MCP tools. `opencode run` loads the project wholesale. One command gives the dispatched session the skill advisor, Code Mode's external-service manuals, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every project-specific plugin. That is the reason you reach for this skill when the task needs project context rather than a model alone.
127: 
128: ### The Two Non-Obvious Rules
129: 
130: Two `opencode run` defaults punish operators who learn them the hard way.
131: 
132: **Rule 1: use `--agent` deliberately.** The live dispatch contract does not support direct top-level routing to `context`, `review`, `debug` or the other subagents the roster names. None of them is directly invokable as a top-level `opencode run --agent` route. Do not pass `--agent general`. The default path is selected by omitting `--agent`. Some small-model paths documented in `SKILL.md` carry narrower omit-agent caveats.
133: 
134: **Rule 2: append `</dev/null` to every non-interactive run.** Without closed stdin, `opencode run` hangs at zero percent CPU after the snapshot-cleanup line. A foreground `| tail` bypasses this because the upstream pipe stage provides closed stdin, but `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` does not. Position `</dev/null` after the prompt argument, before the redirects.
135: 
136: ### The Self-Invocation Guard
137: 
138: If the agent reading this skill is already inside OpenCode, the skill refuses to load. The guard checks three layers in order:
139: 
140: 1. The `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` env var and any `OPENCODE_*`-prefixed vars, which OpenCode sets on session start.
141: 2. Process ancestry, where an `opencode` parent in the tree trips the guard.
142: 3. A best-effort lock-file probe under `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock`, a heuristic layer since that path does not exist on every install.
143: 
144: The one exception is an explicit parallel detached request. When the prompt contains "parallel detached", "ablation suite", "worker farm" or "spawn detached", the guard allows the dispatch because it spawns a separate session id, not a self-dispatch.
145: 
146: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight
147: 
148: Before the first dispatch in a session the skill checks each provider on OpenCode 2 by filtering `opencode models --standalone` for the `<provider-id>/` prefix, or, on OpenCode 1 (fallback), with `opencode models <provider-id>`. The providers, their models and their effort ceilings live in `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster. Restating them here is how the two copies come to disagree. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions) the skill asks before falling back and never substitutes a model you did not approve. The full roster and effort map live in `references/providers-and-models.md`.
149: 
150: ### Agent Delegation
151:

247:

249: |---|---|---|
250: | `command not found: opencode` | CLI not installed or PATH not updated | `brew install opencode` or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install \| bash`, then restart your terminal |
251: | Dispatch hangs at 0% CPU after the snapshot line | Missing `</dev/null` on a non-interactive run | Append `</dev/null` before any `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` redirect |
252: | `--agent general` fails or warns | The default path is selected by omitting `--agent` | Omit `--agent general`. Use `orchestrate` only when it is the documented primary route and help-verified. Route `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` through the documented primary path (or, for `ai-council`, `/deep:ai-council`) instead of a direct top-level `--agent`. |
253: | `provider/model not found` or `401 Unauthorized` | The default provider is not configured on this machine (`llmgateway` on both versions) | Run `opencode providers list` (OpenCode 1) or `opencode models --standalone` (OpenCode 2), then log in the missing provider |
254: | Empty event stream | Output format defaulted to formatted instead of JSON | Force `--format json` |
255: | `Self-invocation refused` | The caller is already inside OpenCode (`OPENCODE_*` env, `opencode` ancestry or a state lock) | Use a different runtime, exit the current session or restate with explicit parallel-detached keywords |
256: | Unknown `--variant` flag on OpenCode 1 | Binary older than the documented baseline | Run `opencode --version` and `opencode run --help`, then upgrade. It has no `run` form on OpenCode 2. See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md) |
257: | Context too large or truncated | The prompt references broad paths instead of specific files | Split large tasks and use `--file` for attachments |

261: ## 8. FAQ
262: 
263: **Q: What does the full-runtime dispatch buy over a sibling cli-* skill?**
264: 
265: A: A sibling cli-* skill dispatches to a single provider's binary. cli-opencode dispatches into a session that loads every plugin, skill and registered MCP server for the project. When the task needs a project-local skill, a project-specific plugin or the skill advisor, only cli-opencode provides all of them in one shot. When it only needs a model, a sibling is leaner.
266: 
267: **Q: When do I need a parallel detached session?**
268: 
269: A: When you are inside OpenCode and want a second session with its own state and session id. Common patterns are an ablation suite across sessions, a worker farm for parallel research and a cross-repo research branch. On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md). The prompt must contain explicit parallel-session keywords or the self-invocation guard blocks the dispatch.
270: 
271: **Q: Why no top-level `--agent`?**
272: 
273: A: OpenCode 2 accepts `--agent general`. OpenCode 1 (fallback) treats named agents like `general` as subagents and will not run them at the top level: it prints a warning, falls back to the default agent and exits 0, so the flag does not select the requested agent. The default agent already covers the general case. For a specific profile, describe the role in the prompt body.
274: 
275: **Q: Why does a non-interactive dispatch hang without `</dev/null`?**
276: 
277: A: OpenCode reads stdin at startup before session creation. When stdout and stderr are redirected to files, stdin stays open and the process waits forever. Appending `</dev/null` provides an immediate EOF so the dispatch continues.
278: 
279: **Q: Which model do I pick?**
280: 
281: A: Default to `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on both versions. On OpenCode 2 (the expected version) the default is `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`, through the same gateway, because v2 lists no `opencode-go` provider unless it is logged in separately. On OpenCode 1 (fallback) that is `--model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max`, through the DevPass LLM Gateway, which fronts the latency-optimized reasoning model at its max thinking tier. The `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent, so that route hangs on "Go usage limit exceeded". One provider now serves both versions. Switch to `minimax/MiniMax-M3` for MiniMax Direct or `openai/gpt-6-sol` for paid premium. The full roster lives in `references/providers-and-models.md`.

19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: cli-opencode applies context-budget semantics to its dispatches. This file records the cli-opencode-specific model windows (§4) and truncation marker syntax (§5), so callers can compose bounded prompts without a second implementation or a drift-prone ruleset.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: Consult this reference when composing a bounded cli-opencode prompt and you need the cli-opencode-specific model windows (§4) and truncation marker syntax (§5).
29: 
30: ### Core Principle
31: 
32: Keep prompts within the selected model window. Apply the truncation marker and eviction discipline below so callers compose bounded prompts without a drift-prone ruleset.
33: 
34: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. WHY CLI-OPENCODE RECORDS BUDGET SEMANTICS
39: 
40: Prompt packs hit the same failure mode when tool output, conversation history, and working memory exceed the selected model window. cli-opencode records the semantics here so callers can compose bounded prompts without adding a second implementation or drift-prone ruleset.
41: 
42: This reference is documentation-only. It does not add runtime budget logic or mutate memory state.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 3. BUDGET DISCIPLINES
47: 
48: Apply these disciplines when composing a bounded cli-opencode prompt:
49: 
50: - budget percentage and working-memory defaults.
51: - file summary thresholds.
52: - fit-to-budget truncation behavior.
53: - priority eviction order.
54: - marker interpretation.
55: 
56: The cli-opencode-specific model windows are in §4. The truncation marker syntax is in §5.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 4. CLI-OPENCODE-SPECIFIC NOTES
61: 
62: The active cli-opencode small-model set is registry-driven, not duplicated here. The relevant windows are:
63: 
64: | Model | Context window | cli-opencode note |
65: | --- | ---: | --- |
66: | `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` (both versions) | Not verified | Default cli-opencode model on both OpenCode versions. The window is not re-verified on this install. Confirm via `opencode models llmgateway` on OpenCode 1, or `opencode models --standalone` filtered for `llmgateway/` on OpenCode 2, before budget-sensitive dispatches. |
67: | `kimi-k2.7-code` | 262,144 | Largest active window (256k via `kimi-for-coding/k2p7`, supersedes the retired `kimi-k2.6`). It is useful for long-file inspection and still follows the budget discipline. At `--variant high` (OpenCode 1 only) cap reads + budget 1200s+ (over-explores broad scopes, observed 2026-06-17). On OpenCode 2 the equivalent is `-m provider/model#high`. The over-exploration behavior is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32. |
68: | `qwen3.6` | 32,000 | Smallest active cli-opencode window. It needs the strictest scope and file anchors. |
69: 
70: Larger windows change what can be retained, not the rule shape. The caller may include more evidence for Kimi-k2.7-code, but should still apply the summary threshold, truncation marker, and eviction priority discipline.
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## 5. TRUNCATION MARKER SYNTAX
75: 
76: The marker syntax is:
77: 
78: ```text
79: [... truncated N tokens]
80: ```
81: 
82: `N` is the estimated token deficit. cli-opencode prompts should treat this as an intentional budget boundary and must not infer hidden evidence. Keep the retained span before the marker.

14: 
15: # OpenCode CLI - Agent Delegation
16: 
17: How cli-opencode routes dispatches to specialized OpenCode agents via the `--agent <slug>` flag. The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes it.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: OpenCode agents are markdown files under `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`. Each file's frontmatter pins the model, tool permissions, system prompt, and behavioral constraints. When `opencode run --agent <slug>` is invoked, the dispatched session inherits all of that.
26: 
27: The cli-opencode skill exposes the project's full agent roster. The calling AI selects the right slug based on the task type. The agent then shapes the dispatched session: different model, different tool permissions, different system prompt.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: - A dispatch needs a role other than the default agent.
32: - The task type picks the slug: codebase exploration, documentation generation, code review, root-cause debugging, or a command-owned research or review loop (§4 maps each to its invocation shape).
33: 
34: ### Discovery commands
35: 
36: | Command | Purpose |
37: |---------|---------|
38: | `opencode agent list` | List all registered agent slugs across project + user scopes |
39: | `opencode debug agent <slug>` | Print resolved frontmatter and system prompt for a slug |
40: | `opencode debug skill <slug>` | Print skill resolution if the agent loads one |
41: 
42: OpenCode loads `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, which in this repository links to `.skilled/agents/`, where the files are edited. On OpenCode 1.19.3, user-level agents fall back from `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`), `~/.opencode/` and `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` when the project file is missing. Which of those OpenCode 2.0.32 reads is unverified. The `debug agent` subcommand prints the merged result so the calling AI can confirm which file the dispatch will load.
43: 
44: ### Orchestration principle
45: 
46: The calling AI decides WHAT to delegate. The agent's frontmatter shapes HOW the dispatched session processes the task. The calling AI always validates and integrates the output.
47: 
48: This separation of concerns is load-bearing for the cli-opencode skill: the calling AI owns the task graph and the integration step, while the dispatched OpenCode session owns the per-task execution under the agent's tool permissions and system prompt.
49: 
50: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
55: 
56: ### Invocation pattern
57: 
58: On OpenCode 1, `--agent <slug>` is valid at the top level ONLY for the primary agent `orchestrate` (and `plan`, an OpenCode built-in), never for `general` (rejected, omit `--agent` instead) and never for a subagent slug (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`) or a command-owned loop executor (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`), all of which route through `--agent orchestrate`'s Task-dispatch or their owning `/deep:*` command (§3-4 below). When `--agent orchestrate` IS used, the flag loads the agent definition from `.opencode/agents/orchestrate.md` (project-local) or the user-level fallback. OpenCode 2.0.32 also accepts `general` and a subagent slug at the top level, but the routing rules in this section still apply there. The dispatch shape pins model, variant, format, and working directory alongside the agent slug:
59: 
60: ```bash
61: # OpenCode 1 only
62: opencode run \
63:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
64:   --agent <slug> \
65:   --variant max \
66:   --format json \
67:   --dir /repo \
68:   "<prompt>"
69: ```
70: 
71: ```bash
72: # OpenCode 2
73: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
74:   --agent <slug> \
75:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
76:   --format json \
77:   "<prompt>"
78: ```
79: 
80: - **Effort:** On OpenCode 1, the `--variant max` flash pin is the cli-opencode default for cross-AI dispatches on the flash default, and `--variant high` stays the generic effort for non-pinned models. On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#<level>` suffix.
81: - **Working directory:** On OpenCode 2 the working directory moves into a `cd`, and a child dispatch needs `--standalone`.
82: - **Provider check:** On this machine, OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider, so confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m`, before the first v2 dispatch (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max`).
83: - **Model precedence:** The agent's own frontmatter may override the model selection if the agent pins a specific model. When an agent does NOT pin a model, the explicit model flag wins, `--model` on OpenCode 1 or `-m` on OpenCode 2.
84: - **Frontmatter effects:** OpenCode 2.0.32 routes a slug the same way and registers the agent's mode, permissions and temperature from its frontmatter. With the `openai-compatible` provider package, the only one tested, it does not send that temperature to the provider, so an agent's `temperature` has no effect there (OpenCode 1 sends it for a primary agent through the same package). Whether it applies those permissions during a run is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.
85: - **Pinned-model test:** No repo agent pins a model, so whether a pinned model beats `-m` on OpenCode 2.0.32 is untested.
86: 
87: ```text
88: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
89:   |
90:   |-- Analyzes task, selects OpenCode agent slug
91:   |-- Constructs opencode run command with --agent <slug> flag
92:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool
93:   |
94:   v
95: opencode run --agent <slug> (EXECUTOR ENTRY)
96:   |
97:   |-- Resolves .opencode/agents/<slug>.md frontmatter
98:   |-- Pins model, tool permissions, system prompt, behavioral rules
99:   |-- Loads project plugins, skills, and MCP servers
100:   |
101:   v
102: OpenCode Session (AGENT EXECUTION)
103:   |
104:   |-- Agent shapes the dispatch under its frontmatter constraints
105:   |-- Streams JSON events (step_start, tool_use, text,
106:   |    step_finish) to the calling AI
107:   |-- Honors LEAF agent restrictions (no nested dispatches, read-only)
108:   |
109:   v
110: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR — RESULT HANDBACK)
111:   |
112:   |-- Parses the JSON event stream
113:   |-- Validates agent output quality
114:   |-- Integrates findings into the parent workflow
115:   |-- Decides next step (next dispatch, completion, escalation)
116: ```
117: 
118: ### Conductor rules
119: 
120: 1. The calling AI always **decomposes** complex tasks before delegating to a single agent.
121: 2. The calling AI always **validates** OpenCode output before integrating.
122: 3. The calling AI never **blindly forwards** user requests to OpenCode without picking the right agent.
123: 4. OpenCode agents operate within their declared tool-permission boundaries. LEAF agents may not write files or dispatch sub-agents.
124: 5. If an agent returns low-quality output, the calling AI retries with refined instructions or selects a different agent.
125: 6. Each `opencode run` invocation is **stateless** by default. Include all necessary context in the prompt or use `--continue` / `--session <id>` for explicit continuation.
126: 7. The calling AI surfaces the JSON event stream to the operator when relevant, especially `tool_use` events.
127: 
128: ### Orchestration boundaries
129: 
130: | Concern | Owner |
131: |---------|-------|
132: | Task selection and decomposition | Calling AI |
133: | Agent slug selection | Calling AI |
134: | Prompt construction (RCAF / TIDD-EC / etc.) | Calling AI |
135: | Model and variant selection | Calling AI (agent frontmatter may pin) |
136: | Tool permissions inside the dispatch | Agent frontmatter |
137: | System prompt and behavioral rules | Agent frontmatter |
138: | Result validation and integration | Calling AI |
139: | Memory handback extraction | Calling AI |
140: 
141: ---
142: 
143: ## 3. AGENT ROSTER
144: 
145: The repo ships these agents under `.skilled/agents/`. Three dispatch classes apply. A fix agent (or operator) MUST route each slug through its correct class, not treat the whole roster as uniformly `--agent`-dispatchable. The summary table below is followed by per-agent property tables for the most-dispatched roles.
146: 
147: | Slug | Class | Role | When to dispatch |
148: |------|-------|------|-------------------|
149: | `general` | Subagent (built-in) on 1.19.3 and 2.0.32. Top-level `--agent` REJECTED on OpenCode 1, accepted on 2.0.32. Use default (omit `--agent`) | Default implementation, complex tasks | Routine multi-step work that does not match a specialist. Never pass `--agent general`, because the default agent already runs when `--agent` is omitted |
150: | `orchestrate` | Primary, directly invokable via `--agent orchestrate` | Multi-agent coordination | Complex workflows that span several agents, or to Task-dispatch a subagent below |

56: ### Invocation pattern
57: 
58: On OpenCode 1, `--agent <slug>` is valid at the top level ONLY for the primary agent `orchestrate` (and `plan`, an OpenCode built-in), never for `general` (rejected, omit `--agent` instead) and never for a subagent slug (`context`, `markdown`, `review`, `debug`, `ai-council`) or a command-owned loop executor (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `prompt-improver`), all of which route through `--agent orchestrate`'s Task-dispatch or their owning `/deep:*` command (§3-4 below). When `--agent orchestrate` IS used, the flag loads the agent definition from `.opencode/agents/orchestrate.md` (project-local) or the user-level fallback. OpenCode 2.0.32 also accepts `general` and a subagent slug at the top level, but the routing rules in this section still apply there. The dispatch shape pins model, variant, format, and working directory alongside the agent slug:
59: 
60: ```bash
61: # OpenCode 1 only
62: opencode run \
63:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
64:   --agent <slug> \
65:   --variant max \
66:   --format json \
67:   --dir /repo \
68:   "<prompt>"
69: ```
70: 
71: ```bash
72: # OpenCode 2
73: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
74:   --agent <slug> \
75:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
76:   --format json \
77:   "<prompt>"
78: ```
79: 
80: - **Effort:** On OpenCode 1, the `--variant max` flash pin is the cli-opencode default for cross-AI dispatches on the flash default, and `--variant high` stays the generic effort for non-pinned models. On OpenCode 2 the effort level rides on `-m` as a `#<level>` suffix.
81: - **Working directory:** On OpenCode 2 the working directory moves into a `cd`, and a child dispatch needs `--standalone`.
82: - **Provider check:** On this machine, OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider, so confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m`, before the first v2 dispatch (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max`).
83: - **Model precedence:** The agent's own frontmatter may override the model selection if the agent pins a specific model. When an agent does NOT pin a model, the explicit model flag wins, `--model` on OpenCode 1 or `-m` on OpenCode 2.
84: - **Frontmatter effects:** OpenCode 2.0.32 routes a slug the same way and registers the agent's mode, permissions and temperature from its frontmatter. With the `openai-compatible` provider package, the only one tested, it does not send that temperature to the provider, so an agent's `temperature` has no effect there (OpenCode 1 sends it for a primary agent through the same package). Whether it applies those permissions during a run is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.
85: - **Pinned-model test:** No repo agent pins a model, so whether a pinned model beats `-m` on OpenCode 2.0.32 is untested.
86: 
87: ```text
88: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR)
89:   |
90:   |-- Analyzes task, selects OpenCode agent slug
91:   |-- Constructs opencode run command with --agent <slug> flag
92:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool
93:   |
94:   v
95: opencode run --agent <slug> (EXECUTOR ENTRY)
96:   |
97:   |-- Resolves .opencode/agents/<slug>.md frontmatter
98:   |-- Pins model, tool permissions, system prompt, behavioral rules
99:   |-- Loads project plugins, skills, and MCP servers
100:   |
101:   v
102: OpenCode Session (AGENT EXECUTION)
103:   |
104:   |-- Agent shapes the dispatch under its frontmatter constraints
105:   |-- Streams JSON events (step_start, tool_use, text,
106:   |    step_finish) to the calling AI
107:   |-- Honors LEAF agent restrictions (no nested dispatches, read-only)
108:   |
109:   v
110: Calling AI (CONDUCTOR — RESULT HANDBACK)
111:   |
112:   |-- Parses the JSON event stream
113:   |-- Validates agent output quality
114:   |-- Integrates findings into the parent workflow
115:   |-- Decides next step (next dispatch, completion, escalation)
116: ```
117: 
118: ### Conductor rules
119: 
120: 1. The calling AI always **decomposes** complex tasks before delegating to a single agent.
121: 2. The calling AI always **validates** OpenCode output before integrating.
122: 3. The calling AI never **blindly forwards** user requests to OpenCode without picking the right agent.
123: 4. OpenCode agents operate within their declared tool-permission boundaries. LEAF agents may not write files or dispatch sub-agents.
124: 5. If an agent returns low-quality output, the calling AI retries with refined instructions or selects a different agent.
125: 6. Each `opencode run` invocation is **stateless** by default. Include all necessary context in the prompt or use `--continue` / `--session <id>` for explicit continuation.
126: 7. The calling AI surfaces the JSON event stream to the operator when relevant, especially `tool_use` events.
127: 
128: ### Orchestration boundaries
129: 
130: | Concern | Owner |
131: |---------|-------|
132: | Task selection and decomposition | Calling AI |
133: | Agent slug selection | Calling AI |
134: | Prompt construction (RCAF / TIDD-EC / etc.) | Calling AI |
135: | Model and variant selection | Calling AI (agent frontmatter may pin) |
136: | Tool permissions inside the dispatch | Agent frontmatter |
137: | System prompt and behavioral rules | Agent frontmatter |
138: | Result validation and integration | Calling AI |
139: | Memory handback extraction | Calling AI |
140: 
141: ---
142: 
143: ## 3. AGENT ROSTER
144: 
145: The repo ships these agents under `.skilled/agents/`. Three dispatch classes apply. A fix agent (or operator) MUST route each slug through its correct class, not treat the whole roster as uniformly `--agent`-dispatchable. The summary table below is followed by per-agent property tables for the most-dispatched roles.
146: 
147: | Slug | Class | Role | When to dispatch |
148: |------|-------|------|-------------------|
149: | `general` | Subagent (built-in) on 1.19.3 and 2.0.32. Top-level `--agent` REJECTED on OpenCode 1, accepted on 2.0.32. Use default (omit `--agent`) | Default implementation, complex tasks | Routine multi-step work that does not match a specialist. Never pass `--agent general`, because the default agent already runs when `--agent` is omitted |
150: | `orchestrate` | Primary, directly invokable via `--agent orchestrate` | Multi-agent coordination | Complex workflows that span several agents, or to Task-dispatch a subagent below |

In a shared tree it belongs to another session, and committing it would publish work you did not write. Even with Layer 2, a commit guarantees `git restore` is a one-command recovery for the target's files if anything escapes the worktree (or if your own orchestration overwrites files in main during artifact sync-back).
155: 
156: ```bash

158: git add <relevant-paths>
159: git diff --cached --name-only
160: git commit -m "chore(wip): snapshot in-flight work before deep-loop dispatch on <target>" -m "Recovery baseline taken before the dispatch, so its writes can be told apart."
161: ```
162: 
163: The commit hash is the recovery baseline. Surface it to the operator before dispatch. When the target has no in-flight changes there is nothing to commit, so `git rev-parse HEAD` is the baseline.

23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: The three sibling cli-* skills exist because their target binaries are external runtimes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot do not own this repo. OpenCode owns this repo. A naive "delegate to opencode" skill makes no sense for an in-OpenCode operator (it would create a circular dispatch).
27:

29:

36: | 3. Cross-AI orchestration handback | OpenCode / Copilot | OpenCode for spec-kit specific workflows | No |
37:

255: ## 5. SMART-ROUTER DECISION TREE
256: 
257: The skill's smart router picks between the three use cases (or refuses) using this decision tree:
258: 
259: ```text
260: INPUT: prompt + calling runtime
261:                 |
262:                 v
263: [ADR-001 SELF-INVOCATION GUARD]
264: - Layer 1: env var lookup (any OPENCODE_* env var present?)
265: - Layer 2: process ancestry (opencode in parent process tree?)
266: - Layer 3: best-effort lock-file probe (~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock present? -- heuristic, not guaranteed on every install)
267:                 |
268:         +-------+-------+
269:         |               |
270:        NO              YES
271:         |               |
272:         v               v
273: [CALLING RUNTIME]   [PROMPT KEYWORDS]
274:         |               |
275:    +----+----+    +-----+-----+
276:    |         |    |           |
277: Anthropic  Other  parallel   self-dispatch
278: (Claude    (OpenCode words    only
279: Code)      Copilot)        |           |
280:    |         |             v           v
281:    v         v        USE CASE 2   REFUSE
282: USE CASE  [PROJECT     (in-       (cycle —
283: 1         SUBSYSTEM    OpenCode   surface
284: (external NAMED?]      parallel)  ADR-001
285: to                      |          error)
286: OpenCode)        +------+------+
287:                  |             |
288:                 YES            NO
289:                  |             |
290:                  v             v
291:              USE CASE 3     USE CASE 1
292:              (cross-AI      (external
293:              handback)      to OpenCode)
294: ```

302: 
303: You are already inside OpenCode (signal: <env|ancestry|lockfile> tripped).
304: Asking cli-opencode to delegate this exact prompt back to OpenCode would create
305: a circular dispatch.

14: 
15: # OpenCode CLI - Unique Capabilities
16: 
17: What `opencode run` brings that the sibling cli-* dispatches do not. Each capability includes the invocation shape and the use case where it pays off. Each shape is shown for OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), with the OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) form beside it where one exists and a link to `./install-and-versions.md` where one does not.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: The sibling cli-* skills (cli-claude-code, cli-codex) dispatch a raw model or external autonomous CLI behind a thin wrapper. The dispatched tool loads no OpenCode project plugin runtime, no OpenCode skills, and no MCP tools unless the calling AI manually attaches files or pastes context.
26: 
27: `opencode run` is different. It spawns a full OpenCode session. That session loads:
28: 
29: 1. Every plugin registered in the project's `opencode.json`
30: 2. Every skill under `.skilled/skills/`
31: 3. Every MCP tool wired through `opencode.json` and `.utcp_config.json`
32: 4. The project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md instructions
33: 5. The project's spec folders and their continuity docs
34: 
35: The cli-opencode skill exists because no sibling provides this. It is the bridge between an external AI and the full plugin / skill / MCP runtime this repo defines.
36: 
37: ### When to Use
38: 
39: - A dispatch needs the project's plugin, skill or MCP runtime (§2)
40: - The task needs a parallel detached session (§3)
41: - The calling AI must parse a structured event stream instead of prose (§4)
42: - The dispatch must run as a named agent definition (§5)
43: - The dispatch must target another repository's runtime (§6)
44: 
45: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 1.19.3 and 2.0.32 on 2026-10-19. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## 2. FULL PLUGIN, SKILL, AND MCP RUNTIME
50: 
51: ### What it does
52: 
53: When `opencode run` starts a session, the runtime loads every plugin, skill, and MCP server the project configures. The dispatched agent has access to:
54: 
55: - All `Skill` invocations the calling AI has access to (system-spec-kit, sk-doc, `sk-code` surface routing, etc.)
56: - All MCP tools (the Skill Advisor's routing tools, and Code Mode's manuals for ClickUp / Figma / GitHub / Notion / Obsidian and the other external services)
57: - Every project-local plugin
58: - The repo's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md instruction set as the system prompt
59: 
60: Whether OpenCode 2 loads the same runtime is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.

94: ## 3. PARALLEL DETACHED SESSIONS
95: 
96: ### What it does
97: 
98: On OpenCode 1, a second `opencode run --port <N>` invocation from inside an existing OpenCode session spawns a separate session with its own session id and its own state directory. Nothing is published: `--share` is a deprecated no-op on 1.19.3, so no dispatch passes it. The original session continues unaffected.
99: 
100: ### Why it matters
101: 
102: For ablation suites, worker farms, and parallel research sweeps, the operator wants N sessions running concurrently. Each session must have:
103: 
104: - A unique session id (not a fork of the parent)
105: - An independent state directory (no shared `messages.jsonl`)
106: - The same plugin / skill / MCP runtime as the parent
107: 
108: The skill's smart router gates this use case behind ADR-001's self-invocation signal. When the signal trips AND the prompt explicitly names a parallel detached session, the router permits the dispatch. Otherwise it refuses (see `./integration-patterns.md` for the full decision tree).
109:

111: 
112: ```bash
113: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3):
114: opencode run \
115:   --port 4096 \
116:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
117:   --agent deep-research \
118:   --variant max \
119:   --format json \
120:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
121:   "Run iteration N of the deep-research loop for the approved spec folder. State file at scratch/iteration-N.jsonl."
122: ```
123: 
124: On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See `./install-and-versions.md`.

422: ## 7. MEMORY HANDBACK
423: 
424: cli-opencode dispatches that produce evidence for a `/speckit:save` continuity write MUST include the Memory Epilogue at the end of the prompt. The dispatched session adds `MEMORY_HANDBACK_START` / `MEMORY_HANDBACK_END` delimiters around a structured JSON payload that the calling AI extracts and feeds to `generate-context.js`.
425: 
426: The full Memory Handback Protocol is shared with cli-claude-code and cli-opencode. See SKILL.md Section 4 (RULES) for the canonical 7-step procedure. The same JSON normalization (camelCase / snake_case aliases) and save gates apply.
427: 
428: ---
429: 
430: ## 8. SINGLE-DISPATCH DISCIPLINE
431: 
432: **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).**
433: 
434: - **Default**: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the work to return, verify outputs exist.
435: - **Kill only the dispatch THIS skill started**: capture its PID at launch (`opencode run ... & OC_PID=$!`) and SIGKILL that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup. (A backgrounded `opencode run &` is not a process-group leader, so a group kill would miss it. Kill the captured PID directly.)
436: - **Never blanket-kill**: never a blanket `pkill -9 -f "opencode run"` pattern (see Rule 5), which kills operator-owned sessions too.
437: - **Before the next dispatch**: only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
438: - **Deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole session at start, and iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
439: - **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
